description.value: Resting-state VIM seed-based functional connectivity study comparing essential tremor patients with matched healthy controls and relating connectivity changes to tremor severity.

spans.text: After considering structural and head-motion factors and establishing the accuracy of our seed region, a VIM seed-based functional connectivity (FC) analysis of resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (RS-fMRI) data was performed to characterize the VIM FC network in ET patients.

description.value: Observational, cross-sectional case-control study of essential tremor patients and matched healthy controls; participants were assessed during an initial visit while antitremor medication-naive. Data collection was approved by an ethics committee and informed consent was obtained.

spans.text: Hence, the final subjects for this study included 26 ET patients and 26 age-, sex-, and education-matched HCs.

name.value: Differences in Left VIM seed FC between ET patients and HCs

spans.text: Table 2. Differences in Left VIM seed FC between ET patients and HCs

definition.value: Compared with HCs, ET patients exhibited decreased left VIM-related functional connectivity in the cerebellum and medial dorsal nucleus of the thalamus, and increased left VIM-related functional connectivity in the primary and supplementary motor cortices.

spans.text: Compared with HCs, ET patients exhibited decreased VIM-related FC values in the CBLM

value: Compared with HCs, ET patients displayed VIM-related FC changes, primarily within the VIM-motor cortex-cerebellum circuit, which included decreased FC in the cerebellum and increased FC in the motor cortex.
FC changes in this circuit correlated with tremor severity.

spans.text: These FC changes, which included decreased FC in the CBLM and increased FC in the MC, were correlated with tremor severity (Fig. 4A,B).
